data.title: Anthropic's IPO turns tech researchers into overnight millionaires
data.description:
By Cory Weinberg
 
When Christopher Kirchhoff, a former Pentagon official, joined Anthropic for a three-month fellowship in 2024, he was surrounded in the corporate lunchroom by “bookish” young technology workers who peppered him with questions about national security, he said.
 
The company only had hundreds of employees at the time, and he said he was awed by what people posted in internal Slack channels about what they were working on. He remembered one employee showing colleagues an early demonstration of artificial intelligence performing basic computer tasks, including buying a Nike sweatshirt online and shipping it to Anthropic’s office without human intervention. “Everyone knew it was a door to the future,” Kirchhoff said.
 
 
That relatively small circle of workers is now in line for enormous paydays.
 
On Thursday, Anthropic vaulted into one of the world’s most valuable companies, after its record-setting initial public offering. That has created sudden, enormous wealth for hundreds of employees who had an early hand in its assent.
 
The bulk of the wealth the company created during its rise will go to a relatively small group of people, who joined it in the early years when Anthropic was worth far less. Anthropic’s investor prospectus ahead of the IPO not only reflected how rapidly it has grown — it had 940 employees at the end of 2024 and about 5,300 as of September — but also showed that those 940 employees stood to gain the most.
 It is unclear just how wealthy many of these employees have become, but Anthropic’s prospectus provides some idea of what employees who joined just two years ago would have coming their way. An employee awarded options on $1 million of stock in 2024 would now, on average, be sitting on about $66 million of stock once it vests, according to a New York Times analysis of the prospectus. Employees who joined earlier would be worth more. But even people who started a year ago might find themselves millionaires on paper now. 
The company started trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, following what was the largest IPO in history that valued Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion less than six years after its founding. Its shares opened notably higher than the $83 a share level set in its IPO, briefly pushing the company’s value over $2 trillion.
 
It reached that value more quickly than other tech companies. Anthropic’s crossing of the $1 trillion mark was more than a decade faster than it took other tech titans, including Meta, Google and SpaceX. Many of the IPO’s biggest winners are the kinds of employees Anthropic has said were a priority to hire in its early days: technically savvy engineers and scientists who believed in the race to rapidly — and responsibly — develop AI in the near future. Anthropic’s founders have encouraged them to donate a portion of their stakes to charity, with the company matching the shares that employees pledged. Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive, said last week on the company’s investor road show that a key to its success was focusing on hiring people who were “oriented toward the public benefit” rather than “jerks.” 
“We’ve been very disciplined about turning down people who are deeply technically talented but don’t fit our culture,” he said. Dr. Amodei and his six co-founders, who made an emotional split from OpenAI during the pandemic in 2020, each own Anthropic stakes now worth more than $20 billion.
 
Employees who joined in 2024 might have had little reason, from the outside, to imagine how big the company would become. It had generated only about $41 million in sales the previous year and hadn’t yet attracted many brand-name venture capital investors to give their seal of approval.
 
As Anthropic has grown, it has actively sought out employees with more typical tech backgrounds and business-focused ambitions. The company wrote in its prospectus, for instance, that it planned to hire more sales people.
 
Many early employees have grown increasingly alarmed about the potential havoc that advanced AI could cause as companies like Anthropic continue to develop it. Some signed an online petition in July urging the US government to lead an effort that would “pace” AI development to ensure proper safeguards are in place. 
Nicholas Joseph, an early employee responsible for training Anthropic’s model, pointed out in the petition that work was being done by AI itself, rather than by humans. “I’m not sure if or where it tops out, but a rapid acceleration in capabilities might be dangerous for society,” he wrote.
 
Driving those fears now is the same calculus that attracted early AI believers to Anthropic — that the technology was going to keep developing. Lillian Li, a tech investor at the Scottish fund manager Baillie Gifford, remembered meeting Anthropic executives for the first time in 2023. She had heard initially about the company’s potential from AI researcher friends, all of whom had a sense that “the next five years were going to look very different.”
 
“They were very earnest and sincere people that wanted to do good for the world and no one had taken seriously prior to that,” she said.

data.title: Dilip Buildcon share price surges 7% on ₹419-crore Gurugram Metro order win
data.description:
Shares of Dilip Buildcon surged over 7 per cent in morning trade on Thursday, driven by the company's announcement of an order win.
 
The stock opened higher at ₹402 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and extended gains to hit an intraday high of ₹424.70.
 
The rally marked the second consecutive session of gains for Dilip Buildcon shares. The stock has advanced nearly 8 per cent over the two sessions.
 
However, the stock pared more than half of its early gains as the session progressed. As of 9:45 AM, Dilip Buildcon shares were trading 3.07 per cent higher at ₹398 on the NSE, with nearly 3 million shares changing hands. Dilip Buildcon wins ₹419.47 crore order 
 
According to an exchange filing by Dilip Buildcon, it has received a Letter of Acceptance for the tender floated by the Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL). 
 
The project involves the construction of depot cum workshop including civil works, architectural works, and E&M works, for the elevated corridor of Gurgaon Metro at Sector 33. 
ALSO READ: Stock Market LIVE: Sensex off lows, Nifty reclaims 25,500; Nifty IT rises 2%
 
The total value of the order is worth ₹419.47 crore and the project will be executed in a period of 21 months. 
Dilip Buildcon stock: Technical view Harish Jujarey, AVP, head - technical equity research, Prithvi Finmart, said that Dilip Buildcon stock price is broadly trading with a sideways over the past few weeks. Towards the end of October, the stock tested its previous swing low support around ₹360 and witnessed a mild recovery, with prices currently hovering near ₹400.
 Going ahead, the ₹360 zone remains a crucial support. On the upside, the 200-DMA at ₹425, followed by the falling trendline around ₹430, will act as immediate resistance. Overall, the stock is likely to remain range-bound. A decisive breakout on either side will provide further directional cues, he said. Dilip Buildcon Q2FY27 results  
Dilip Buildcon is a Bhopal-based construction and infrastructure company.  During the September quarter of FY27, the company reported a PAT of ₹101 crore in Q2FY27, compared with ₹214 crore in Q2FY26, which included exceptional items of ₹122 crore.
 
Its consolidated revenue from operations in the September quarter stood at ₹2,250 crore, compared with ₹1,926 crore in the year-ago period. Ebitda was at ₹439 crore in the reporting three-month period, while margin stood at 19.5 per cent.
 
As of September 30, 2026, Dilip Buildcon said that its order book stood at a record ₹33,081 crore, up 19 per cent from ₹27,691 crore as of June 30, 2026 and 15 per cent from ₹28,830 crore as of March 31, 2026. 
 
As of September 30, 2026, Dilip Buildcon’s standalone net debt stood at ₹2,146 crore.

data.title: Anthropic pares IPO gains as shares slide 5% in after-hours trading
data.description:
By Natasha Mascarenhas, Carmen Reinicke and Sangmi Cha
 
Anthropic PBC shares were down about 5 per cent in post-market trading as the artificial intelligence developer wrapped up its first day as a public company after a record-setting $107.3 billion offering. 
The late moves pared a debut pop of 17 per cent on Thursday, which provided a rare bright spot as the Nasdaq fell 2.2 per cent. The broader market continued on a downward trend into the Asian day, with global stocks poised for their longest losing streak in more than three years, as the AI trade cratered. 
 
While the bright open for the Claude chatbot maker reflected massive investor appetite after a heavily oversubscribed initial public offering, the steep valuation — combined with fresh competitive threats — weighed heavily in after-hours trading, highlighting jitters over how long that momentum can hold.
 
 
“With what appeared to be the final pillar supporting the AI rally now giving way, market sentiment is now very pessimistic,” said Gerald Gan, chief investment officer at Singapore-based Reed Capital. “While I am preparing to accumulate quality stocks at more attractive valuations, I am equally mindful of the risks of catching a falling knife.”
 
MSCI Inc.’s Asia Pacific equities index fell 3.4 per cent, extending its decline to a seventh session, and is poised for its lowest close since April. That pushed the MSCI All Country World Index — a key barometer of global stocks — on course for its longest losing streak since September 2023.
 
Against that backdrop, Anthropic’s IPO had attracted global demand for seven times the shares available for sale, with investors outside the US pouring in billions of dollars, including those in Japan securing $3 billion in stock after seeking $9.4 billion in shares and $1.1 billion of stock bought by mom-and-pop investors in the UK and continental Europe. 
The IPO vaulted Anthropic to the status of unrivaled AI industry leader — at least for the moment — and delivered billions of dollars in returns to its backers and pushed up the combined wealth of its seven founders to $166 billion. The record raise blasted by the $75 billion IPO record set in June by SpaceX, which ultimately totaled $86.25 billion with the so-called overallotment shares sold by the underwriters. Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Morgan Stanley and 20 other banks earned a record $550 million in fees for their work on Anthropic’s IPO.
 
Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut followed weeks of shaky trading in US stocks, which has left investors grappling with worries over Nvidia Corp.’s role as a major backstop of the AI ecosystem following its longtime chief’s ouster and a Democratic sweep in midterm elections that promises to change the industry’s regulatory landscape.
 
“You’ve seen sentiment sort of continue to worsen around AI and it has not let up today,” said Jordan Watson, managing director of investments at Tandem Investment Advisors. “What’s important for markets now is Anthropic is the most transparent real-time signal of the AI risk trade.”  
Anthropic closed at $97.17 Thursday in New York, paring an opening surge that took it as much as 39 per cent above the IPO price of $83. It ended the day as the world’s seventh-biggest public company with a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion.
 
In a blow to sentiment, Apple Inc. said it is developing its own autonomous AI agent that can get things done on behalf of users, looking to enter a fast-growing market already being pursued by Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta Platforms Inc. and others.
 
Thursday’s broader market weakness was “just a continuation of what we’ve seen for the last several weeks, and that is a lot of nervousness around the semiconductor space,” said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth. “The financing of the AI ecosystem is certainly a question that investors are asking and it’s weighing on the market at large.”
 
Some of the broader selloff may have also been fueled by investors selling positions in other companies to buy Anthropic shares, she added.  
The company won over investors with a focus on enterprise customers, propelling its run-rate revenue — a measure annualized from a shorter period — to $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, its regulatory filings show.
 
Claude Code, the company’s coding agent for software developers, is widely adopted in the industry and has even been used by NASA engineers, the filing shows. Anthropic has more than 11,900 customers delivering $100,000 of revenue each on a trailing 12-month basis as of the end of September, up from about 1,500 in 2025.
 
The company aims to expand its footprint in more professions from law to healthcare. Anthropic counts Novartis AG CEO Vas Narasimhan as one of its board members.
 
A major challenge will be taming ballooning costs for AI infrastructure and reliably delivering operational profitability. Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss in the third quarter, primarily driven by $5 billion of computing costs under short-term commitments and $2 billion of non-cash charges related to the company’s charitable donation-matching program.
 
“It popped like any other IPO on the first day but we will need to see solid results in the coming quarters, new use cases for AI, accelerating monetization etc to dispel the gloom in the AI trade,” said Vey-Sern Ling, managing director at Union Bancaire Privee. “Investors don’t have very many fundamental drivers to go on for Anthropic for now. A large part of the value is in the future, which is uncertain, so the share price movements will reflect that.”
 
Goldman Sachs Group Inc. research analysts expect the company to take until 2030 to generate positive free cash flow on an annual basis, Bloomberg News reported. That said, they are modeling Anthropic’s annual revenue to soar to roughly $685 billion by 2030, Bloomberg News has reported. To pull off that feat, it will need to fend off AI pricing pressures from cheaper open-weight models, including from Chinese developers.
 
Anthropic is expected to see a lift from index-tracking funds generating billions of dollars in demand. If it qualifies for early inclusion, it could join the Russell 1000 and the Nasdaq 100 as soon as December. FTSE Russell and Nasdaq changed their rules this year to speed the inclusion of large new listings.

data.title: Gold at 15% discount, silver at 28%: DSP steps up precious metals exposure
data.description:
DSP Mutual Fund is preparing to increase its exposure to gold and silver through its DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds, setting staggered buying levels to accumulate the metals if international prices decline further.
 
The fund, which has maintained an exposure of around 10% to gold and almost no exposure to silver against a benchmark allocation of 20% to precious metals, has started reducing this underweight position. Its benchmark allocation comprises 15% gold and 5% silver.
 
In an investor communication dated November 18, the fund said it had begun a rules-based accumulation strategy, under which it would add small amounts of gold and silver at predetermined price levels rather than chase rising prices. 
Decide the allocation rules in advance. Execute when prices reach predefined levels. This removes the need to make fresh decisions during market volatility.
 
 
For silver, the fund has started with an allocation addition of 0.5% of the portfolio at prices just below $47 an ounce. It plans to add another 0.5 percentage point for every $2 per ounce decline. Once silver falls below $42, it intends to accelerate purchases to 1% tranches, along with an additional one-time 0.5 percentage point purchase.
 
According to the fund's illustration, a decline in silver prices from $47 to $37 an ounce would result in cumulative additions of 5% to the portfolio.
 
For gold, the fund plans to add 0.5 percentage point of portfolio exposure at prices close to $3,850 an ounce, followed by another 0.5 percentage point for every $100 per ounce decline. The subsequent buying levels are $3,800, $3,700, $3,600 and so on.
 
The fund said the objective was not to predict the bottom of the market but to accumulate systematically as prices decline. It may slow down or accelerate purchases depending on market conditions. If prices do not fall further, it may not add aggressively or could reconsider the strategy.
 
Why is the fund changing its stance?
 
DSP said it had maintained a significant underweight position in precious metals since the fund's launch, even as several comparable multi-asset strategies remained neutral or overweight.
 
Its exposure stood at approximately 10% in gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs), with almost no silver exposure, against the benchmark's 20% allocation. The fund had briefly held 0.5% in a silver ETF, bought in June 2026 when international silver prices were around $56 an ounce and sold near $70.
 
The fund now believes valuations offer a more attractive entry point, although it would prefer a larger discount to its estimated fair value before making substantial additions.
 
According to DSP's valuation framework, gold was trading at approximately $3,799.8 an ounce against its estimated fair value of $4,484, implying a discount of 15.3%. Silver was trading at around $46 an ounce against an estimated fair value of $64, a discount of 28.4%.
 
The framework uses factors including the stock of above-ground gold, US and European money supply, and the historical gold-to-silver ratio. For silver, it uses a gold-to-silver ratio of 60 to derive a theoretical price range of $53-$75 an ounce, with a midpoint of $64.
 
The fund said it would ideally like to see a discount of more than 20% to its theoretical fair-value estimates. Its staggered buying plan is designed to build exposure at progressively lower prices rather than make a large allocation at current levels.
 
These are the fund's own valuation estimates and assumptions, not universally accepted measures of the intrinsic value of gold or silver. 
Gold prices are at a 15% discount to our framework prices, while Silver is at a 28% discount.
 
Five factors shaping the precious metals strategy
 
DSP has outlined five broad considerations behind its decision to begin accumulating precious metals.
 
First, it is looking for a meaningful discount to its estimated fair value. While silver's discount was already around 28%, gold's was approximately 15% in the fund's calculations.
 
Second, it is watching whether at least one of three major sources of demand — jewellery buyers, central banks or ETFs — becomes a stronger incremental buyer. The fund said central-bank purchases were stable but not rising, ETF demand remained strong, and jewellery demand was weak. It expects jewellery demand could stabilise following a correction in prices.
 
Third, it is tracking the US dollar index (DXY). A stronger dollar could put pressure on precious metals prices and create opportunities for the fund to add at lower levels. DSP described dollar strength as a short-term headwind and one of the factors that could help its accumulation strategy.
 
Fourth, for silver, it is monitoring the gold-to-silver ratio. The fund began its additions when the ratio was close to 82 and said it would prefer levels above the 80-85 range, alongside the other conditions in its framework.
 
Finally, it is looking for signs of rapid selling followed by lower participation in futures and ETF markets. DSP said gold and silver were showing some of their most oversold readings, although prices could become even more oversold.
 
Import duty changes could alter buying pace
 
The fund has also identified changes in India's import duty on precious metals as a factor that could influence its purchases.
 
According to DSP, the effective import duty on gold and silver was increased from 6% to 15% on May 13, 2026. The nine-percentage-point increase raised domestic landed costs by approximately 8.5%, assuming international prices and exchange rates remained unchanged.
 
A reduction or removal of the duty could lower domestic gold and silver prices, including the net asset values (NAVs) of ETFs holding these metals. DSP said such a move could create more attractive entry points for fresh purchases and may prompt it to accelerate accumulation, depending on valuations and market conditions.
 
The fund said the additional allocation to gold and silver would largely be funded by reducing debt exposure and rebalancing some equity-sector allocations.
 
For investors, the shift is significant because it marks a change in the fund's asset-allocation stance after an extended period of underweight exposure to precious metals. However, the proposed purchases are conditional on prices and market signals. The fund has not announced an immediate move to its full benchmark allocation or a fixed timeline for completing the process.
 
The strategy is specific to DSP Multi Asset Omni Fund of Funds and should not be interpreted as a recommendation for investors to increase their own gold or silver holdings.

data.title: Rupee strengthens 17 paise to 93.15 against US dollar in early trade
data.description:
The rupee appreciated 17 paise to 93.15 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday, backed by robust foreign fund flows into domestic equity markets and a retreating greenback against major rivals.

Forex traders said the local unit showed resilience despite higher crude oil prices and negative sentiment in domestic stock markets.

At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.25 and gained further to trade at 93.15 against the greenback, up 17 paise from its previous close.

On Thursday, the rupee rallied for the fourth straight session and settled 9 paise higher at 93.32 against the US dollar. In the preceding three sessions, the domestic currency gained 78 paise or 0.83 per cent since the closing level of 94.19 recorded on November 13.

 

Anuj Choudhary from Mirae Asset Sharekhan said the rupee is expected to trade with a slight positive bias on overnight decline in crude oil prices and sharp fall in gold and silver prices, which may ease import bills.

"Softening of US Treasury yields may also support the rupee. However, a strong dollar and hawkish Fed speak may cap sharp gains. USD-INR spot price is expected to trade in a range of Rs 92.85 to Rs 93.40," he added.

Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.76, lower by 0.07 per cent.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.40 per cent higher at USD 92.35 per barrel in futures trade.

On the domestic equity market front, Sensex declined 217.03 points or 0.26 per cent to 82,804.72 in early trade, while Nifty fell 58.70 points or 0.23 per cent to 25,455.60.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 7,411.41 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data.

data.title: Anthropic founders' combined wealth jumps to $166 bn after record IPO
data.description:
By Dylan Sloan
 
Anthropic PBC’s record-breaking IPO has pushed the combined wealth of its seven co-founders to $166 billion as shares of the AI lab jumped following its debut.  ALSO READ: Anthropic becomes world's 7th most valuable company with $1.8 trn valuation 
The stock, which priced at $83 a share, closed Thursday at $97.17 in New York trading, valuing each founder’s fortune at about $24 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. The $107.3 billion public offering and concurrent private placement broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever.   
ALSO READ: Anthropic's IPO turns tech researchers into overnight millionaires
 
The group first became billionaires less than two years ago after the San Francisco-based company raised $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion valuation. Another funding round that closed in May propelled all seven onto Bloomberg’s ranking of the world’s 500 richest people. 
ALSO READ: Anthropic IPO: 5 things to know about the record $81.3 billion listing
 
 
The Claude chatbot maker has an unusually even ownership structure among its founders, with each holding about the same 1.3 per cent fully diluted economic stake in the firm. That makes the seven the largest number of individuals appearing on Bloomberg’s wealth index who work at any one company.
 
Despite their relatively small economic stakes, the founders retain outsized control over the company through Founder LLC, an entity that owns a single Class F share carrying 50.1 per cent of Anthropic’s voting power. They will retain those voting rights as long as they collectively hold at least 2 per cent of the Class A shares they owned at the time of Anthropic’s public debut.
 
All seven have pledged to dedicate 80 per cent of their personal company equity to philanthropic causes. Anthropic’s prospectus specifies that these commitments aren’t legally binding and constitute voluntary, revocable pledges.

Paper Wealth

Anthropic’s offering is a key step in the AI industry’s massive wealth boom. According to a recent Bloomberg Businessweek analysis, founders and employees at San Francisco-based AI startups together hold more than $1.2 trillion in company equity. 
 
Although much of that paper wealth remains tied up in illiquid private company shares, Anthropic’s public debut will allow founders and employees to cash out hundreds of billions of dollars in company stock.
 
That process won’t be immediate: Lock-up restrictions outlined in Anthropic’s prospectus prevent current and former employees from selling shares for as long as six months. The co-founders face an even longer lock-up period of up to a year.
 
Anthropic’s leadership is already taking some money off the table. Each of the seven co-founders sold shares worth about $280 million in the IPO, according to the prospectus. In addition, both Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive officer, and his sister, Daniela, its chair, participated in tender offers in June 2025 and April 2026, according to the prospectus.
 
Other co-founders include Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah.
 
Anthropic’s strong opening also boosted the net worth of Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao to about $1.1 billion. Rao, who joined the company in 2024 after roles at Airbnb Inc. and Blackstone Inc., holds about 9.3 million vested stock options.
 
Founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI employees, Anthropic was valued at $461 million in its Series A funding round that year, according to PitchBook. Since then, its valuation has climbed more than 320,000 per cent, based on the fully diluted valuation implied by the offering price.
 
That rapid rise and the resulting explosion of insider wealth come as tech titans account for a growing share of the world’s ultra-wealthy. Through the first nine months of the year, tech billionaires on Bloomberg’s wealth index added a combined $845 billion to their fortunes, while everyone else on the list lost a combined $62 billion.

data.title: Aadhaar card not conclusive proof of date of birth, rules Delhi HC
data.description:
The Delhi High Court has held that an Aadhaar card alone cannot conclusively establish a person's date of birth, Bar and Bench reported.
 
In an order passed on November 13, Justice Manoj Kumar Ohri rejected a plea by JJ Electronics against a labour court decision that refused to accept an employee's Aadhaar details as definitive evidence of her age.
 

What was the case?

 
The dispute arose after JJ Electronics terminated the services of Rosamma Joy, an employee who worked as a “finishing man”, a year before her scheduled retirement.
 
The company found a mismatch in her year of birth across two records. While her Aadhaar card mentioned 1959, the details submitted to the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) listed 1960 as her year of birth.
 
 
On the basis of the Aadhaar entry, the management maintained that Joy had reached the retirement age of 58 and ended her employment. Joy subsequently approached the labour court, challenging the termination and seeking reinstatement along with full back wages.
 
The labour court declined to rely on the Aadhaar card as conclusive evidence of her age, noting that no witness from the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) had been examined to establish the basis on which her date of birth was recorded. 
ALSO READ: Delhi's AQI improves to 269, Gurugram's air remains most polluted in NCR
 
The court instead accepted 1960 as Joy's year of birth, as reflected in the EPIC records, and directed the company to provide back wages and consequential benefits. JJ Electronics then challenged this decision before the Delhi High Court.
 

What did the High Court rule?

 
Upholding the labour court's decision, the high court said the legal framework governing Aadhaar establishes its use as proof of identity, not as conclusive evidence of a person's date of birth.
 
The court observed that the law governing Aadhaar recognises the Aadhaar number as proof of identity, but not as proof of date of birth. It also referred to a 2018 office memorandum issued by UIDAI, which states that the date of birth recorded on an Aadhaar card is based on documents or a self-declaration submitted by the cardholder.
 
The High Court accepted Joy's argument and observed that she had not reached the age of superannuation in 2017. It pointed out that the ESIC records listed her date of birth as May 20, 1960, and held that the employer could not use a different date mentioned in her Aadhaar card to bring forward her retirement by a year.
 
It also agreed with the labour court's finding that her termination was illegal because JJ Electronics had not followed the relevant provisions of the Industrial Disputes Act.

data.title: Urban Company raises ₹2,500 crore via QIP; issue subscribed over 6 times
data.description:
Home services platform Urban Company on Thursday said it has raised ₹2,500 crore through a Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) of equity shares, with the issue getting bids worth over ₹15,000 crore, or about six times the issue size.
 
The QIP, which opened on November 16 and closed on November 19, saw participation from more than 60 investors. The company allotted 16.02 crore equity shares at ₹156 apiece to 33 investors.
 
The issue price represented a 3.1 per cent discount to the floor price of ₹161.03 per share, calculated under Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) regulations.
 

Who participated in Urban Company's QIP?

 
Urban Company received bids from more than 60 investors. Shares were allotted to 33 of them, 13 of which did not hold the company’s shares on the date of the issue. These included SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Kotak Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund.
 
 
Domestic insurers such as HDFC Life, Bajaj Life Insurance and Edelweiss Life also participated in the issue.
 
Global institutional investors included Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Pictet, Amundi, Norges Bank Investment Management, Manulife, Dymon Asia and Millennium. Domestic investor Premji Invest also participated.
 
Of the 33 investors allotted shares, 13 did not hold Urban Company shares on the date of the issue.
 

How will Urban Company use the ₹2,500 crore?

 
According to the placement document, the company plans to deploy the net proceeds across several business areas.
 
A significant portion will go towards strengthening the supply ecosystem for InstaHelp by UC, its service offering. The funds will also support brand marketing, business promotion, technology and cloud infrastructure, and training infrastructure for service professionals.
 
Urban Company will also use the proceeds for research and development of native products, potential acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
 
Morgan Stanley India Company was the lead book-running manager for the QIP, supported by Kotak Mahindra Capital Company and Emkay Global Financial Services.

data.title: Nifty Metal drops 3% as firm dollar dents base metals; APL Apollo top loser
data.description:
Metal stocks came under pressure on Friday, with the Nifty Metal index falling nearly 3 per cent in intraday trade as a firm US dollar and a sharp correction in global base metal prices weighed on investor sentiment. 
 
The Nifty Metal index, which tracks the performance of companies operating in the metal and mining sectors, declined 2.59 per cent to 11,980 at intraday trade.
 
At the last check, 14 of the 15 index constituents were trading in the red, with APL Apollo Tubes leading the losses. The counter was down over 5 per cent to ₹2,040. Vedanta Aluminium Metal and Tata Steel followed, declining around 3 per cent each.
 
 
Hindustan Zinc, Vedanta Aluminium Metal, JSW Steel, Hindustan Copper, and SAIL dropped between 1.5 per cent and 2 per cent, among others. 
 
Sunny Agrawal, head, fundamental research at SBI Securities, said, “We believe that metals are discounting the hawkish stance by the US Fed, and the appreciation of the dollar Index is an indication of the same.”
 
He added that the correction in metal prices has also been aggravated due to the narrative of a likely slowdown in AI related capex. Copper prices are trading at a 7-month low. The supply-related disruption premium in aluminium can reduce materially if there is no flare-up of tensions in the ME. Basically, correction in the prices of base metals and precious metals is putting pressure on the metal stock prices, he said.
 
LME aluminium prices have declined 6.5 per cent month-to-date (MTD), while LME copper has seen a sharper fall of 11.5 per cent over the same period.
 
The sharp decline in aluminium and copper prices is likely to have a mixed impact across sectors. Lower prices could weigh on realisations and margins of metal producers such as Vedanta, NALCO and Hindustan Copper, while benefiting downstream users, including cable and wire makers, electrical equipment manufacturers, consumer durables and auto component companies, through lower input costs.
 
Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market, said that the Nifty Metal index is moving south in a lower lows and lower highs formation after hitting all-time highs in May–June 2026. At the current juncture, it is trading around its one-year exponential moving average (12,000 levels), and a decisive close below this could drag it towards the 11,600–11,400 spot zone. Conversely, sustained trading above 12,250 levels could start a pullback rally towards 12,500–12,650 levels.

data.title: Flipkart's Big Billion Days sale timing weighs on Walmart's Q3 growth
data.description:
US-based retail giant Walmart has said it faced a 100-basis-point headwind to its top-line growth in the third quarter as the 'Big Billion Days' sales event of its Indian e-commerce arm Flipkart shifted to the fourth quarter this year.

"Timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days ("BBD") event negatively affected growth with an expected corresponding benefit to Q4," said Walmart in its earnings statement.

The company saw the impact as Flipkart's 11-day Big Billion Days (BBD) festive sale shifted to a different timing compared with that of the previous year, with its sales contribution shifting to Walmart's fourth-quarter results.

"As we previewed on last quarter's call, we faced a 100-basis-point headwind to top-line growth in Q3 due to the timing of Flipkart's Big Billion Days event, or BBD in India, which will be reported in International's fourth-quarter results this year," said John David Rainey, Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Walmart Inc.

 

The 13th edition of Big Billion Days, which opened on October 9, 2026, recorded 20-22 per cent year-on-year growth in orders, units and buyers, according to reports.

However, Walmart also said this shift will provide a boost of around 100 basis points to its sales growth in the ongoing fourth quarter. The impact is expected to reverse in the December quarter, when the sales contribution from the event will be reflected in Walmart's international segment.

In the third quarter, Walmart, which follows the February-January fiscal calendar, said, "Timing of BBD negatively affected net sales growth by about 500 bps" in its international business, which operates in 18 countries outside the US, including India.

Walmart International's "e-commerce sales down 2 per cent and advertising business down 15 per cent, both negatively affected by timing of BBD," said the Bentonville, Arkansas-headquartered retail giant in its earnings statement for the third quarter of FY27.

In the zone, excluding Flipkart, inventory is growing slower than sales, it added.

Walmart International has reported a growth of 7 per cent to $35.9 billion in the third quarter of FY27. In terms of constant currency, Walmart International's growth was only 3.3 per cent to $34.7 billion.

"Growth driven primarily by India and China, with business mix benefits, partially offset by strategic investments in Mexico and Canada," it said.

The overall revenue of Walmart Inc. was $188.8 billion, up 5.2 per cent in Q3 FY27.

Walmart has also raised its full-year FY27 net sales growth outlook to 4.9-5.2 per cent, in constant currency, from its earlier estimate of 4-5 per cent.

"Net sales for FY27 are expected to grow 4.9 per cent to 5.2 per cent and adjusted operating income to grow 8 per cent to 8.6 per cent, all in constant currency," it said.
